# 17: vLLM inference backend

**What to build:** Rollouts are generated by vLLM instead of the Hugging Face
generate loop, while training stays on the Hugging Face model with the LoRA
adapter. The choice is a config value, default stays Hugging Face, so the
existing path is untouched.

**Blocked by:** None. Builds on the one update per step change.

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] A config value selects the inference engine, `hf` or `vllm`, default `hf`, with clear rejection of anything else.
- [ ] The vLLM backend implements the same generator contract and returns the same generation objects, with reasoning and code split by the existing parser.
- [ ] The backend samples n answers per prompt in one call, at the configured temperature and completion cap.
- [ ] Old logprobs are still recomputed on the training model during the update pass, so the vLLM path does not depend on engine logprobs.
- [ ] The LoRA weights reach the engine once per optimizer step, through one documented sync method, and never per prompt.
- [ ] Selecting vLLM without the package installed fails with one clear message and does not affect the `hf` path.
- [ ] The `hf` path stays the default and its behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] Tests drive the backend through a fake engine. No GPU and no network at test time.
- [ ] Docs describe the trade and the sync strategy.

## Notes

- vLLM is inference only. It cannot train. The training model keeps its own copy of the weights and the adapter.
- The engine needs the adapter or the merged weights after every optimizer step. That sync is the hard part and the main risk. Keep it behind one small adapter class so a future vLLM version only changes that class.
- At 0.6B the two copies fit together on a 48 GB card alongside activations.
- Memory reporting and the reward path are unaffected.
